The plugin-hostd protocol
=========================

The plugin-hostd protocol is a superset of mod-host's text protocol: any mod-host client works unchanged.

Protocol `plugin-hostd`, version 1 of its JSON declaration (`protocol/plugin-hostd.json`); mod-host's protocol as the daemon models it is `protocol/mod-host.json`, version 1, written from the mod-host headers `mod-host.h`, `protocol.h`, `host-errors.h` the daemon is built against. The verbs the daemon adds are declared in `data/verbs.json` (since 0.12.0, requiring omx-contract-schema >= 3.12.0, omx-clap-core >= 0.30.5).

1. Transport
------------

| what | value | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| command port | TCP, 5555 without `-p` | the command port without -p; the feedback port is the next one, unless -n is given |
| feedback port | TCP | the next port after the command port, unless -n is given; `-f <port>` names it |
| daemon ready | `plugin-hostd ready!` | printed on stdout once both ports accept |
| worker ready | `ready!` | the end of the line a worker prints once its socket accepts |
| worker command line | `-n -p <command port> -f <feedback port>` | how the daemon starts every worker |
| line_max | 4096 bytes | the protocol socket's buffer: the longest pin_set line the daemon takes |
| line_words_max | 64 words | the words of one command line the daemon reads, the verb included; a word past them is not read |
| string_max | 255 bytes | the longest string word |

A command is one line of words, the verb first; a reply is `resp <code> [...]`: the words after the code are the verb's reply grammar below, and a negative code is a refusal, named in [Reply codes](#reply-codes). Events go out on the feedback port, one line each ([4. Events and feedback](#4-events-and-feedback)).

Discovery: the daemon declares itself in files, not on the socket. The verb tables below are installed as:

| file in this tree | installed as |
|---|---|
| `grammar/plugin-hostd-protocol.abnf` | `/usr/share/plugin-hostd-protocol/plugin-hostd-protocol.abnf` |
| `protocol/mod-host.json` | `/usr/share/plugin-hostd-protocol/mod-host.json` |
| `protocol/plugin-hostd-protocol.json` | `/usr/share/plugin-hostd-protocol/plugin-hostd-protocol.json` |
| `protocol/plugin-hostd.json` | `/usr/share/plugin-hostd-protocol/plugin-hostd.json` |
| `protocol/plugin-hostd.schema.json` | `/usr/share/plugin-hostd-protocol/plugin-hostd.schema.json` |

`pkg-config --variable=protocoldir plugin-hostd-protocol` names that directory, and `--variable=table`, `grammar` and `protocoljson` name the files. The `protocol` and `version` keys of the protocol JSON identify it; `hello` answers the version on the socket ([Sessions](#sessions-hello-and-request-tags)).

The verb table and the grammar
------------------------------

`protocol/plugin-hostd-protocol.json` is the one table of the protocol: every command, each once, with its origin, its argument types, its reply and its refusals, and every feedback line. It is merged from `protocol/mod-host.json`, `protocol/plugin-hostd.json`, `data/verbs.json`, `include/plugin-hostd/omx_clap_core_host_verbs.h` by `tools/protocol-table.py`; 48 commands of origin mod-host, 28 commands of origin plugin-hostd, 11 commands of origin omx-clap-core, 6 commands of origin plugin-hostd-protocol, 21 feedback lines.

`grammar/plugin-hostd-protocol.abnf` is the grammar of a line, in ABNF (RFC 5234, with RFC 7405's case-sensitive strings): the lexical core, written once by hand (`grammar/core.abnf`), and a rule per command, per feedback line and per parse refusal generated from the table by `tools/abnf-gen.py`. Every line of the scenario corpus and every reply the library writes in the golden transcript is held to it (`make test-grammar`).

A word of another origin that mod-host also has either extends mod-host's command (takes its arguments, in its types, first, and more only where mod-host's command takes a tail), or is a second form of the word told apart from mod-host's by its number of arguments, so that a line of mod-host's form is always answered as mod-host answers it. Any other is refused: the table is not written, and there is no list of exceptions. The words with more than one form:

| verb | form | origin | reply | codes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `add` | `add word int ...` | mod-host | as mod-host answers it | - |
| `add` | `add word int` | plugin-hostd | as mod-host answers it | - |
| `add` | `add word int placement` | plugin-hostd | as mod-host answers it | - |
| `add` | `add word int word` | plugin-hostd | as mod-host answers it | - |
| `add` | `add word int placement word` | plugin-hostd | as mod-host answers it | - |
| `preset_show` | `preset_show word` | mod-host | as mod-host answers it | - |
| `preset_show` | `preset_show int word` | plugin-hostd | resp 0 <json> | -523 PRESET_NOT_OFFERED; -524 PRESET_INVALID; -3 reply.host.instance-non-exists; -901 reply.host.memory-allocation; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation |
| `supervisor_reset` | `supervisor_reset` | plugin-hostd | as mod-host answers it | - |
| `supervisor_reset` | `supervisor_reset worker` | plugin-hostd | as mod-host answers it | - |
| `supervisor_reset` | `supervisor_reset all` | plugin-hostd | as mod-host answers it | - |

Sessions: hello and request tags
--------------------------------

A client that never sends `hello` is answered exactly as mod-host answers it: that is mod-host mode, and it is how mod-ui and Zynthian's engine talk to a host. `hello` opens a session that may use what mod-host's protocol lacks, each part named as an extension. The lines, from the grammar:

```abnf
cmd-hello                = %s"hello" SP int tail
hello-reply      = %s"resp" SP %s"0" SP int [SP ext-tags] [SP ext-errors] [SP ext-seq]
extension        = ext-tags / ext-errors / ext-seq
ext-tags         = %s"tags"
ext-errors       = %s"errors"
ext-seq          = %s"seq"
request          = [tag SP] command
answer           = [tag SP] reply
tag              = "@" 1*tag-char
tag-char         = ALPHA / DIGIT / "-" / "_" / "."
event            = [seq SP] feedback
seq              = "#" %x31-39 *DIGIT
error-reply      = %s"resp -1 reply.host.instance-invalid" / ...
```

- The client names the protocol version it speaks and the extensions it asks for: `hello 1 tags errors seq`. The daemon answers with its own protocol version and, of the extensions asked for, the ones it grants, each once and in the order of the table below: `resp 0 1 tags errors seq`. An extension the daemon does not know is not granted, and is no error.
- The version is the one the protocol JSON carries. It changes only when a word, a code or the shape of a verb changes incompatibly; what is added comes as a new extension. A client checks the version and uses only the extensions granted.
- A version that is not a whole number of 1 or more is refused with -902, and nothing changes.
- Each `hello` replaces what the one before it granted, so `hello 1` alone goes back to mod-host mode. A new connection starts with nothing granted.
- A host that does not know `hello` answers `not found`, as mod-host does, and one that grants nothing may refuse it with -902; on any answer but `resp 0` the client stays in mod-host mode. A host built on this library answers it once it calls `protocol_add_hello()`.

| extension | what it grants |
|---|---|
| `tags` | request tags: a line may start with @<tag>, and its answer then starts with the same @<tag> |
| `errors` | error words: a refusal resp <n> is followed by the stable word of its code, reply.<group>.<reason>, when the protocol declares one |
| `seq` | event sequence numbers: every feedback line starts with #<n>, 1 for the first after this hello and one more for each, so a gap is a missed line |

### Request tags

In a session granted `tags`, a request may start with a tag: `@` and one or more letters, digits, `-`, `_` or `.`, then one space, then the command. Its answer, a reply or a parse refusal, starts with the same tag and one space:

```
> @a7 param_get 3 gain
< @a7 resp 0 0.2500
> @a8 remove
< @a8 few arguments
```

- A line without a tag is answered without one. Answers still come in the order of the requests; the tag lets a client match them without counting.
- A tag with nothing after it is answered `<tag> not found`.
- A first word that starts with `@` but is not a tag (`@` alone, or with any other character) is read as a verb, and answered `not found`. So is every line that starts with `@` in a session not granted `tags`, as mod-host answers it.
- The answer to a tagged `hello` carries its tag, also when that `hello` drops `tags`.
- Events and feedback lines go out on the feedback port and never carry a tag, also when a tagged request caused them.

### Error words

In a session granted `errors`, a refusal `resp <n>` is followed by one more word, the code the protocol declares for that number: a stable word that is never reworded, which a client can match and translate without a table of numbers. The number stays first, so a client that reads only the number reads it as before:

```
> param_get 9 gain
< resp -3 reply.host.instance-non-exists
```

- The words are those of the [reply codes](#reply-codes), 50 numbers in all; a number the protocol declares no code for goes out bare.
- Only a refusal alone gets its word: a reply that carries values after its number, a success and a parse refusal (`not found`, `few arguments`, which are words already) go out as they are.
- With `tags` as well, the tag comes first: `@a9 resp -3 reply.host.instance-non-exists`.

### Event sequence numbers

In a session granted `seq`, every line on the feedback port starts with its number, `#` and a whole number, then one space: 1 for the first line after the `hello` that granted `seq`, one more for each line after it. A number that is not one more than the last one read is a line the client missed:

```
< #1 output_set 3 level 0.25
< #2 output_set 3 level 0.5
< #4 output_set 3 level 0.75     (line 3 was missed)
```

- A `hello` that grants `seq` again starts the numbers again at 1; one that drops it drops the numbers.
- A line the host could not send keeps its number, so the client sees the gap.
- Requests and answers on the command port carry no number; an event a tagged request causes carries its number and no tag.

Bulk verbs
----------

A bulk verb does in one line what a client would send once an instance or a parameter. It is a verb like any other and needs no `hello`: it changes no line a client already sends, and a host that does not serve it answers `not found`, as mod-host does, or -902. A host built on this library answers them over its backend once it calls `host_dispatch_register()`. `param_set_many` is all or nothing: every pair is checked before any value is set, and a line refused answers `resp <code> <position>`, the first refused pair's code and its position from 1.

| verb | form | reply | codes | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `param_get_many` | `param_get_many int word ...` | `resp 0 <value> ...` | -3 reply.host.instance-non-exists; -103 reply.host.param-symbol-invalid; -901 reply.host.memory-allocation; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | The values of several parameters of one instance in one line: <instance> <symbol> [<symbol> ...], each value as param_get writes it, in the order asked. A symbol the instance does not have refuses the whole line with param_get's code (-103), an instance that does not exist with -3, and no value is answered then. |
| `param_set_many` | `param_set_many int word float ...` | `resp 0` | -3 reply.host.instance-non-exists; -103 reply.host.param-symbol-invalid; -901 reply.host.memory-allocation; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | Several parameters of one instance in one line, all or nothing: <instance> <symbol> <value> [<symbol> <value> ...]. Every pair is checked before any is set: a symbol the instance does not have (-103), an instance that does not exist (-3), a value that is not a number or a pair with no value (-902). The first pair refused refuses the line, answered resp <code> <position> with the pair's position from 1, and no value is set. Should the host refuse a value as it sets it, the values set before it are set back, and the line is refused the same way. |

`param_get_many`:

```
> param_get_many 3 gain cutoff :bypass
< resp 0 0.2500 440.0000 0.0000
> param_get_many 3 gain nope
< resp -103
```

`param_set_many`:

```
> param_set_many 3 gain 0.5 cutoff 880
< resp 0
> param_set_many 3 gain 0.75 nope 1 cutoff 440
< resp -103 2     (nothing is set: gain stays 0.5)
```

Curves
------

A panel description's display (an EQ's response, a dynamics stage's transfer curve) is drawn from the instance itself. The controller binds the display once, when the panel opens: `curve_bind` names, for each role the description gives the display, the parameter that plays it, its unit and, for a band's type, the band shape of each choice value. A binding may take more than one line, as a line is at most 64 words and a 32-band EQ's binding is 160 terms: each line adds its terms, and a line of another kind or family starts the binding again. Then each `curve_points` reads every bound parameter from the instance as it is at that moment, with the rate the instance runs at, and answers the points omx-dsp's `omx_curve_points` draws, the one curve function every surface calls. The host keeps the binding with the instance, drops it with the instance's remove and never saves it; it judges nothing of it. A host built on this library answers both verbs once it calls `host_dispatch_register_curve()` with the rate of its instances; one that does not answers -902, and mod-host answers `not found`: a surface then draws the display's frame alone.

| verb | form | reply | codes | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `curve_bind` | `curve_bind int int word ...` | `resp 0` | -3 reply.host.instance-non-exists; -103 reply.host.param-symbol-invalid; -536 CURVE_KIND_UNKNOWN; -538 CURVE_UNIT_REFUSED; -901 reply.host.memory-allocation; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | Bind a display of an instance's panel description to the instance's parameters, for curve_points: <instance> <display> clear, or <instance> <display> <kind> <family> <term> [<term> ...], the display's index in the description, its kind (eq_response or transfer_curve) and family, and each term <role>[.<index>]=<symbol>[:<unit>][@<shape>\|<shape>...] as the description gives the role: the parameter that plays it, its unit, for a band_type the band shape of each choice value from 0 (a band_freq takes one shape, the band's fixed shape), and for a head filter's slope the dB per octave of each choice value from 0 (@12\|24), the role's declared enumeration. The terms are added to the display's binding, a term of a role and index already bound replacing it; a line of another kind or family starts the binding again, and clear drops it. Every term is checked before any is kept: an instance that does not exist (-3), a symbol it does not have (-103), a family with no closed form for the kind (-536), a unit the role does not take (-538), a term the grammar does not take (-902). The binding lives with the instance and goes with its remove; it is never saved. |
| `curve_points` | `curve_points int int int` | `resp 0 <count> <x>,<y> ...` | -3 reply.host.instance-non-exists; -103 reply.host.param-symbol-invalid; -536 CURVE_KIND_UNKNOWN; -537 CURVE_TERM_MISSING; -539 CURVE_POINTS_RANGE; -542 CURVE_VALUE_NOT_FINITE; -901 reply.host.memory-allocation; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | The points of a bound display: <instance> <display> <points>, the grid points asked for. Each bound symbol's value is read from the instance as it is now and the instance's rate with it, and omx-dsp's omx_curve_points draws them: an eq_response x in Hz and y in dB, the bands' anchors added (three a drawn band), a transfer_curve input dB to output dB. The reply is the count and each point x,y, x to four significant digits and y to 0.01 dB, ascending in x; at most curve_points_max (omx-dsp's CURVE_POINTS_MAX, 256) points. A display with no binding, or a binding without a term the model needs (-537); a band shape or slope with no closed form (-536); points outside 2 to curve_points_max, the anchors counted (-539); a value that is not finite or an instance not running at a rate (-542). |

A term is `<role>[.<index>]=<symbol>[:<unit>][@<shape>|<shape>...]`: the role word and the band's index as the description gives them, the parameter's symbol (a host's own control starts with `:`), the unit token, and the shapes (`off`, `bell`, `lowshelf`, `highshelf`, `highpass`, `lowpass`, `notch`, or `-` for a choice value with no closed form). The words are omx-dsp's `CURVE_ROLES`, `CURVE_UNITS` and `CURVE_SHAPES`; the grammar spells them as `curve-term`. A reply carries at most omx-dsp's `CURVE_POINTS_MAX` points, 256, an EQ's three anchors a drawn band among them, so a caller asks for 256 less three times the drawn bands at most.

```
> curve_bind 3 0 eq_response eq band_freq.0=f_0:hz band_gain.0=g_0:coef band_q.0=w_0:oct band_type.0=ft_0@off|bell|lowshelf|highshelf
< resp 0
> curve_bind 3 0 eq_response eq band_freq.1=f_1:hz band_gain.1=g_1:coef band_q.1=w_1:oct band_type.1=ft_1@off|bell|lowshelf|highshelf
< resp 0
> curve_points 3 0 128
< resp 0 134 20.00,0.00 20.54,0.00 ...
> curve_bind 4 0 transfer_curve dynamics threshold=thr:dbfs ratio=ratio:ratio knee=knee:db makeup=gain:db
< resp 0
> curve_points 4 0 1
< resp -539
> curve_points 4 1 64
< resp -537     (display 1 has no binding)
```

Monitors
--------

`monitor_output` starts the feedback lines of an output (`output_set`, on the feedback port). A monitor ends with the connection that set it: a controller that disconnects, or whose connection drops, leaves none behind, and the next connection starts with none, so it asks again for the outputs it wants. `monitor_output_off` ends one earlier, and only the connection that set a monitor can end it: an output this connection did not monitor is refused (-543). A host built on this library keeps what each connection monitored and calls the callback given to `host_dispatch_register_monitor_output_off()` for the output a `monitor_output_off` ends, and for every output still monitored when the connection ends or its instance is removed; a host that does not register it answers -902, and mod-host answers `not found`.

| verb | form | reply | codes | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `monitor_output_off` | `monitor_output_off int word` | `resp 0` | -543 OUTPUT_NOT_MONITORED; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | Ends the monitor monitor_output set on an output: <instance> <symbol>, answered resp 0, and the output's feedback lines stop. A monitor ends with the connection that set it, so a controller that disconnects leaves none behind, and only the connection that set a monitor ends it earlier: an output this connection did not monitor (never monitored, monitored by an earlier connection, already ended, or its instance removed) is refused (-543), and a line that is not an instance and a symbol, or a host that does not serve the verb, is refused (-902). The output's ledger line goes with the monitor, so a respawn of the instance does not replay it. |

```
> monitor_output 3 level
< resp 0
> monitor_output_off 3 level
< resp 0
> monitor_output_off 3 level
< resp -543     (already ended)
```

2. mod-host's verbs on plugin-hostd
-----------------------------------

`required` is answered as its grammar says; `optional` is answered, or refused with -902, and never misread; `absent` is refused on purpose, and no client of the profile may need it.

Answer: `same` is relayed to the worker that holds the instance (any other verb to every worker) and answered as that worker answers it; `differs` is a verb plugin-hostd declares a grammar or a behaviour of its own for, or one the Path A run observed answered otherwise on the LV2 worker; `refused` is absent of every profile. The argument types are mod-host's templates (`int` %i, `word` %s, `float` %f, `...` an optional tail); the declarations carry no unit per argument, and a range or a unit a verb has is in its meaning.

mod-host's templates name no reply codes per verb: a relayed verb answers what its worker answers, or one of -503 WORKER_SPAWN (the worker is not up: the spawn failed, or it is in backoff; ask again after instance_restored) or -507 VERB_DROPPED (the worker died on this very command and the daemon dropped it: it is not replayed, and the instance_verb_dropped event names it; or it died on, or did not answer in rpc_timeout_ms, the pin_expect of an add, which is then never forwarded).

| `track_info` | int word word ... | optional (every profile) | differs | plugin-hostd declares it: `<instance> <name> <#RRGGBB \| -> [bus \| return \| master]` → `resp 0`; the strip's name ("" for none), colour and kind, absent for an input channel; a worker whose plugin format has a track-info extension passes them on; any other word is -902, and so is a name of 256 bytes or more, one that is not UTF-8 as RFC 3629 spells it (an overlong form, a surrogate, a code point past U+10FFFF, a lead byte without its tails) or one that holds a control character of Unicode's class Cc: U+0000 to U+001F, U+007F or U+0080 to U+009F |

| `remote_page_get` | int int | optional (every profile) | differs | plugin-hostd declares it: `<instance> <page>` → `resp 0 <page_id> <section> <page_name> <s1> <s2> <s3> <s4> <s5> <s6> <s7> <s8>`; one page, 0 to count - 1: each slot the symbol param_set takes, - for an empty one; -902 for a page that is not one |
| `param_info` | int word | optional (every profile) | differs | plugin-hostd declares it: `<instance> <symbol>` → `resp 0 <unit> <scale> <min> <max> <default> <step> <stable_symbol>`; what a parameter's value means: its unit, its scale, and the symbol it keeps across hosts and versions; -103 for a symbol that is not a parameter, the plugin's own bypass and :bypass included; -511 for a parameter whose unit and scale the worker holds no checked contract for |
| `help` | none | optional (every profile) | same | - |

3. Verbs mod-host does not have
-------------------------------

Each is declared in `protocol/plugin-hostd.json`; the formats, codes and hosts come from `data/verbs.json`, or from omx-clap-core's verb table for a verb the two hosts share. A verb whose meaning begins "sent by the daemon to a worker" is the daemon's to a worker, never a controller's.

### Pins and qualification

A path of a pin, and the path of a `clap:` uri, is written percent-encoded (`PHD_PIN_PATH_ESCAPE`): a separator of `pin_set`'s words, whitespace, `%`, a quote, a backslash and a control byte are `%XX`, so any file name is one word (`Surge XT.clap` is `Surge%20XT.clap`). `%` is always an escape: a file name that holds a `%` itself writes it `%25`, and a `%` not followed by two hex digits is refused. A pin is keyed by its `clap:` uri's path decoded: `"clap:/c/Surge XT.clap#id"`, quoted, and `clap:/c/Surge%20XT.clap#id` are one pin, whichever spelling `pin_set`, `pin_clear` or `add` uses, and the pin store writes the decoded path as one quoted word.

| verb | arguments | types | reply | codes | since (the group's) | hosts | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pin_set` | `<uri> <path>=<sha256>[,<path>=<sha256>...] <scheme>:<sha256> [verdict=<verdict>] [pool=<pool>]` | word word word ... | `resp 0` | -516 PIN_REFUSED; -901 reply.host.memory-allocation; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | 0.12.0 | plugin-hostd required | the pin of one plugin: the SHA-256 of every file the host loads for it, a path relative to the bundle (the directory of a single-file format's file), its layout fingerprint and, when they are known, the verdict of its qualification and whether its worker gets the CLAP thread pool; it replaces an earlier pin of the uri; -516 for a plugin whose pins_dir pin carries verdict=refused, which only the user's pin_accept overrides. The pin store, a pin_file and a pins_dir file hold the same line, with or without the verb |
| `pin_clear` | `<uri> \| all` | word | `resp 0` | -901 reply.host.memory-allocation; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation; -540 DURABLE_WRITE_FAILED; -541 WRITER_QUEUE_FULL | 0.12.0 | plugin-hostd required | forget the pin of one plugin, or of every one; a pins_dir pin is read-only and holds again |
| `pin_reload` | none | none | `resp 0` | -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | 0.12.0 | plugin-hostd required | read the pin_file and the pins_dir files again and put the pins in at once, without a restart; the daemon also does this by itself when one of those files changes. Running instances keep running: one the new pins refuse is logged and its id in worker_list is followed by !. The pin_set pins of the controller are kept. -902 under pin_mode off or when the pin_file is gone or has a line outside the grammar, and the earlier pins hold |
| `pin_changed` | `[<uri>] [files \| layout]` | ... | `resp 0` | -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | 0.12.0 | plugin-hostd required | the notice the package sync sends to every daemon it knows after it rewrote the pin file: the same as pin_reload, with or without the pin_changed event's words after it; more words than those are -902 |
| `pin_accept` | `<uri>` | word | `resp 0` | -508 PIN_ABSENT; -509 PIN_BINARY_MISMATCH; -516 PIN_REFUSED; -901 reply.host.memory-allocation; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation; -540 DURABLE_WRITE_FAILED; -541 WRITER_QUEUE_FULL | 0.12.0 | plugin-hostd required | pin_mode first-use only: take the plugin's files as they are now as its pin, after a pin_changed event; the layout is learned again by the next add and the verdict is dropped. Of a plugin whose pin carries verdict=refused (pins_dir or pin_file) it is the user's choice to load it anyway: kept beside the pin store, it runs alone in a worker of its own, pin_clear takes the choice back; -508 when the plugin has no pin, -509 when its files cannot be collected, -902 under pin_mode strict |
| `pin_layout` | `<instance>` | int | `resp 0 <scheme>:<sha256>` | - | 0.12.0 | omx-clap-host optional, mod-host unsupported | sent by the daemon to a worker of a format that checks layouts, after it accepted the add of a plugin whose layout pin is still unknown: the layout the worker found after init, which the daemon records in the pin |
| `pin_expect` | `<instance> <scheme>:<sha256>` | int word | `resp 0` | -1 reply.host.instance-invalid; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation; -508 PIN_ABSENT | - | plugin-hostd unsupported, omx-clap-host required, mod-host unsupported | sent by the daemon to a worker of a format that checks layouts, just before the instance's add: the layout pin that add checks after init and before activate; any other reply than resp 0 refuses the add with that code, and the add is never forwarded |

### Chains and plans

| verb | arguments | types | reply | codes | since (the group's) | hosts | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chain` | `<chain> <instance> [<instance> ...]` | int int ... | `resp 0` | -518 CHAIN_UNKNOWN_INSTANCE; -519 CHAIN_DUPLICATE; -520 CHAIN_INSTANCE_BUSY; -521 CHAIN_MIXED_FORMAT; -501 PLACEMENT_INVALID; -901 reply.host.memory-allocation; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | 0.12.0 | plugin-hostd required, omx-clap-host required, mod-host unsupported | the instances, in this order, are one chain, run in one worker of place chain:<chain>: each member's state is saved, it is removed from the worker it was in and replayed in the chain's. A chain already declared takes the new order, and a member left out of it goes back to a worker of its own; while its worker is up that worker is kept: a new member joins it (its add, the order, its state, its ledger, its connections) and no other member is restarted, unless the new member's format narrows the worker's world, which forms the chain again. Members of clap and lv2-clap form one chain. A worker that runs chains in one client (clap, lv2-clap) is sent this line, with the members it holds, after the adds of its replay; one that does not (mod-host) never is. A worker that refuses the line would not run the members as one: the chain is forgotten and each member runs in a worker of its own, the line answers -501, and the event chain_refused carries the worker's own code, also when the refusal comes later, on a respawn. Every instance verb still names one member by its own number. A member that crashes the worker is quarantined to a worker of its own and the chain goes on without it; quarantine_clear puts it back. -518 for an instance no add made, -519 for one named twice, -520 for one in another chain, -521 for members no one worker program runs together, -501 for a plugin that may not share a worker while require_pins is on (a CLAP plugin whose first-use pin is not in-process; an LV2 member whose bundle is not found, since a chain's worker sees a world narrowed to the union of its members' bundles), -902 for a chain or an instance that is not a number, or fewer than chain_members_min (1) instances |
| `chain_clear` | `<chain>` | int | `resp 0` | -522 NO_SUCH_CHAIN; -901 reply.host.memory-allocation; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | 0.12.0 | plugin-hostd required | forget the chain: each member goes to a worker of its own; -522 for a chain no chain declared |
| `chain_get` | `<chain>` | int | `resp 0 <worker> <instance>,... <instance>,...` | -522 NO_SUCH_CHAIN; -901 reply.host.memory-allocation; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | 0.12.0 | plugin-hostd required | read a chain back: its worker (- when it has none), its members in the declared order, and the members its worker runs now in their order (- for none); a quarantined member is declared and not running; -522 for a chain no chain declared, -902 for a chain that is not a number |
| `plan` | `<chain> <instance> [<instance> ...]` | int int ... | `resp 0 <instance>,...;<instance>,...;... <core>,...;<core>,...;...` | -518 CHAIN_UNKNOWN_INSTANCE; -519 CHAIN_DUPLICATE; -520 CHAIN_INSTANCE_BUSY; -501 PLACEMENT_INVALID; -901 reply.host.memory-allocation; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | 0.12.0 | plugin-hostd required | the instances, in signal order, are planned (the grouping-planner design note): the daemon decides, from the pin and the cost of each, which runs of consecutive members share a worker. A run of two or more is declared as a chain of place chain:<chain>.<k>, k counting segments from 0; a member that shares with no neighbour is placed own. The reply names the segments in order, the members of one joined by commas and the segments by semicolons, then the cores: the segments again with each member replaced by the audio core of the worker that runs it now, - for one the setting placement did not pin (docs/placement.md). A chain planned again keeps the running worker of every segment that did not change, and the daemon plans it again by itself when a member is quarantined and, history_regroup_s after a death that split its group, to gather it. The plan numbers are its own, apart from chain's. While the setting grouping is off the plan is answered and kept for plan_get and nothing moves. A segment that cannot be formed refuses the whole plan with its own code, moves nothing and is told by plan_get as plan-refused:<code>. A segment its worker refuses, which is known only once it has moved, refuses the plan with -501 too, and then every segment ends and each member runs in a worker of its own. -518 for an instance no add made, -519 for one named twice, -520 for one in a chain or in the plan of another chain, -501 for a segment no world can be built for or its worker refuses, -902 for a chain or an instance that is not a number, or fewer than chain_members_min (1) instances |
| `plan_get` | `<chain>` | int | `resp 0 <instance>,...;<instance>,...;... <instance>:<reason>,... <core>,...;<core>,...;...` | -532 NO_SUCH_PLAN; -901 reply.host.memory-allocation; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | 0.12.0 | plugin-hostd required | read the last plan of a chain back: its segments as plan answered them, then the members that have a reason, instance:reason joined by commas (- for none); the reasons are the words of PLUGIN_HOSTD_GROUPING_REASONS (data/grouping.json), then the cores of the members as plan answers them; -532 for a chain no plan planned, -902 for a chain that is not a number |
| `plan_clear` | `<chain>` | int | `resp 0` | -532 NO_SUCH_PLAN; -901 reply.host.memory-allocation; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | 0.12.0 | plugin-hostd required | forget the plan: each member goes to a worker of its own; -532 for a chain no plan planned |
| `estimate` | `<rate> <quantum> <uri> [<uri> ...]` | int int word ... | `resp 0 <latency_frames> <cpu_percent> <ram_bytes> <workers> <unknown_count> <member>:<code>,... <ram_used_bytes> <ram_added_bytes> <ram_budget_bytes> <ram_unknown_count>` | -533 NO_RECORD; -534 NO_CELL; -535 UNKNOWN_PLUGIN; -901 reply.host.memory-allocation; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | 0.12.0 | plugin-hostd required | what a chain of these plugins, in signal order and named as add names them, would cost at that rate and quantum, read from the qualification records of qualification_dir; no plugin is loaded and nothing moves. latency_frames adds up each member's measured latency of the grid point, else its declared one; cpu_percent adds up each member's median nanoseconds per sample times the rate, percent of one core's cycle (a member's cost per block over the block's duration); ram_bytes adds up the Pss of the worker each member ran alone in, the history's pss_mb_solo of the binary its pin holds on this host class, - unless every member has one, since no qualification record carries a RAM figure; workers is how many workers plan would place the members in (an isolated one alone); unknown_count is how many members have no figure at that rate and quantum, and the latency and the CPU add up only the others. The last word names each of them as its position in the line, from 0, and its code, -533 for no record, -534 for no point of the grid at that rate and quantum, -535 for a uri that names no plugin installed here, joined by commas, - for none. Several records of one plugin (several versions) give the largest figure. -902 for a rate or a quantum that is not a whole number above 0, or no uri |

< resp 0

```
> estimate <rate> <quantum> clap:/usr/lib/clap/omx-comp.clap#org.openmixer.comp
< resp 0 <latency_frames> <cpu_percent> <ram_bytes> <workers> <unknown_count> <member>:<code>,... <ram_used_bytes> <ram_added_bytes> <ram_budget_bytes> <ram_unknown_count>
```

| verb | arguments | types | reply | codes | since (the group's) | hosts | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `descriptor_get` | `<uri>` | word | `resp 0 "<path>"` | -528 DIR_NOT_WRITABLE; -529 DESCRIPTOR_ABSENT; -530 DESCRIPTOR_PENDING; -531 DESCRIPTOR_SCAN_FAILED; -901 reply.host.memory-allocation; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | 0.12.0 | plugin-hostd required | the scanned descriptor of the plugin, answered from descriptor_dir: the file named for its binary as it is now (<id>@<version>-<hash>.json), written by the scan the plugin's add ran. -529 when there is none, -530 while its scan runs, -531 when its last scan wrote nothing, -528 when the directory could not be written |
| `panel_get` | `<uri>` | word | `resp 0 "<path>"` | -528 DIR_NOT_WRITABLE; -529 DESCRIPTOR_ABSENT; -530 DESCRIPTOR_PENDING; -531 DESCRIPTOR_SCAN_FAILED; -901 reply.host.memory-allocation; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | 0.12.0 | plugin-hostd required | the panel the plugin publishes (org.openmixer.panel-description/1), answered from descriptor_dir: the file panels/<id>@<version>-<hash>.json, named as its descriptor, which the same scan writes once the descriptor is in place, {"plugin": {"format", "id"}, "panel": <the panel object omx-clap-scan --json prints for the plugin, null when it serves none>}; an LV2 plugin's panel is null. The codes are descriptor_get's: -529 when there is none, -530 while its scan runs, -531 when its last scan wrote nothing, -528 when the directory could not be written |
| `history_get` | `<uri>` | word | `resp 0 <history>` | -901 reply.host.memory-allocation; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | 0.12.0 | plugin-hostd required | what the daemon kept of the plugin on this host class, for the binary its pin holds now (the running history: the windows it ran alone and in a group, its crashes, restarts and quarantines): one word of comma-joined digest=<sha256>, class=<host class>, crashed=<0\|1>, raises_xruns=<0\|1> and then every key=value of the record (data/history.json); - when the plugin has no pin or no record, unavailable while the history file is blocked or history_window_s is 0, -902 for a line that is not one word |

### The plugin's own window

`show_external_ui <instance>` puts the plugin's own window on the display and `hide_external_ui <instance>` takes it off, as jalv and mod-host show one; both are optional of every profile. The daemon sends each to the worker that holds the instance and returns the worker's resp as it wrote it: omx-clap-host answers `resp 0`, or `-404` and a `hosting.window.*` code when no window shows. `-902` comes back when the instance's worker has no window (mod-host's, an LV2 instance on the `lv2` row) or the worker does not know the verb. The window belongs to the worker's display session, the `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` or `DISPLAY` of the daemon's environment, which every worker inherits; a daemon with neither answers `resp -902 hosting.window.no-display` and sends the worker nothing. The ledger keeps the latest of the two per instance: a window that was shown is shown again after a respawn, after the state, and a hidden one is not.

| verb | arguments | types | reply | codes | since (the group's) | hosts | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hide_external_ui` | `<instance>` | int | `resp 0` | -3 reply.host.instance-non-exists; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | - | plugin-hostd optional, omx-clap-host required, mod-host unsupported | take the plugin's own window off the display, kept for the next show_external_ui; answered as show_external_ui is, resp 0 also when no window is shown; in the ledger it takes back the show, so a respawn shows nothing |

`hide_external_ui`:

```
> hide_external_ui 0
< resp 0
```

### The node's name in the graph

A hosted node's client stays `effect_<instance>`; its pretty-name, JACK metadata on the client's uuid, is `<plugin name> (<instance>)` (`node_metadata`). `node_label <instance> <label words>` makes it `<label>: <plugin name> (<instance>)`, and `node_label <instance>` with no words clears the label. The daemon sends the verb to the worker that holds the instance, which sets the metadata; the ledger keeps the latest, so a respawned worker is labelled again, and `remove` ends it (plugin-hostd#35).

| verb | arguments | types | reply | codes | since (the group's) | hosts | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `node_label` | `<instance> [<label word> ...]` | int ... | `resp 0` | -545 LABEL_INVALID; -3 reply.host.instance-non-exists; -902 reply.host.invalid-operation | 0.12.0 | plugin-hostd optional, omx-clap-host optional, mod-host unsupported | label the node for graph clients: the worker that holds the instance sets its pretty-name to the labelled form of PHD_NODE_METADATA, the label the words joined by one space; no words clears it, back to the plain form. -545 for a label over PHD_NODE_LABEL_MAX bytes or not UTF-8; the ledger keeps the latest, so a respawned worker is labelled again (plugin-hostd#35) |

`node_label`:

```
> node_label 0
< resp 0
```

4. Events and feedback
----------------------

mod-host's feedback lines, relayed as the worker wrote them:

| line | arguments |
|---|---|
| `output_set` | int word float |
| `remote_pages_changed` | int |

The daemon's events and the worker lines it relays:

| event | fields | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `worker_died` | `<worker> <pid> <exit:N \| signal:N> <instance>,...` | a worker died; the instances it held, or - for none |
| `instance_verb_dropped` | `<instance> <the command as sent>` | the command a worker died on, dropped from the ledger; or the add it died on, the add as the worker was given it, which names the plugin, or the pin_expect of that add |
| `instance_verb_dropped` | `<instance> suspect:<ms> <the command as sent>` | the last verb a worker answered when it died inside suspect_window_ms, <ms> the age of the reply |
| `worker_backoff` | `<worker> <ms>` | the respawn waits this long |
| `worker_respawned` | `<worker> <pid> <replayed_count> <ms>` | a worker is back and its ledger replayed |
| `instance_restored` | `<instance> <worker>` | an instance is back in a worker |
| `instance_replay_refused` | `<instance> <code>` | a replayed add was refused, by its pin or by the worker, <code> the refusal's own: no worker holds the instance until the next replay |
| `instance_quarantined` | `<instance> <worker>` | the culprit of a pool or a chain death, placed own until cleared; a chain goes on without it |
| `chain_formed` | `<chain> <worker> <instance>,...` | a chain's worker is up with these members, in this order, after its declaration, a respawn or a member's quarantine; - for none. <chain> is the number chain declared, or <plan>.<k> for segment k of a plan |
| `chain_refused` | `<chain> <code>` | a chain's worker would not run the members as one chain, <code> its own answer, and its stderr says why: the chain is forgotten and each member runs in a worker of its own. <chain> as chain_formed names it |
| `chain_stalled` | `<chain> <instance \| -> <step> <code>` | a chain, or a plan's segment, has not formed within chain_form_timeout_ms of its declaration: the member and the step that held it (spawn, add, pin, state, memory) and the code it answered, 0 for none, - for no one member; said once each time it is declared or gathered again, and the daemon goes on trying |
| `plan_reason` | `<chain> <instance>:<reason>,...` | a plan of the chain changed: the reasons plan_get answers now, after the segments, - for none |
| `supervisor_gave_up` | `<worker> <deaths> <window_ms>` | the storm bound is spent; respawning ends |
| `pin_changed` | `<uri> files \| layout` | an add or a replay of a plugin was refused because its files, or the layout the worker found, differ from its pin; the pin is as it was until pin_accept or pin_set |
| `lv2_adapter_refused` | `<uri> <reason> omx-clap-host` | the LV2 adapter of the lv2-clap worker refused a plugin: <reason> is the hosting.* code after -102 on the worker's reply to that add (- when it named none); the last word is the lv2_worker in force, omx-clap-host, and the add is answered (-512) |
| `remote_pages_changed` | `<instance>` | relayed from a worker: the plugin changed its remote pages; read them again |
| `remote_page_suggest` | `<instance> <page_id>` | relayed from a worker: the plugin suggests the remote page of that id (a page_id of remote_page_get); a surface may follow it |
| `param_gesture` | `<instance> <symbol> begin \| end` | relayed from a worker: the user took hold of a control of the plugin's own, or let it go; a controller writes no automation of that parameter in between. The values the plugin moves meanwhile, or at any time by itself, are mod-host's param_set feedback lines, relayed as written. A gesture whose worker died, or whose instance was removed, before its end is ended by the daemon, before the worker_died event |
| `xruns` | `<count>` | relayed from a worker, and read by the daemon: the JACK xruns the worker has counted since it started, written when the count changes and at most once a second; a worker that never writes it counted none. The daemon takes the first count of a worker as its baseline and, at the close of each history window, adds the window to xrun_windows_solo or xrun_windows_grouped of every member of the worker when the count rose in it; a line that is not the word and one whole number is not a count |
| `abi_clobber` | `<instance> <mask> <registers> <call> <block>` | relayed from a worker (omx-clap-host 0.26.2 or later), and read by the daemon: the plugin returned from a call with a callee-saved register changed, said once per instance. The worker put the registers back, so its own frame is whole; the other members' state in the same process is not covered, so the daemon quarantines the instance (instance_quarantined, and the history keeps it alone from then on) and, when it shares its worker or is in a chain, moves it to a worker of its own with its state saved; one already alone is only marked |
| `param_set` | `<instance> <symbol> <value>` | relayed from a worker: parameter feedback, a value the plugin moved by itself (its automation, an LFO, a preset load, a MIDI map, the user's knob of the plugin's own), as mod-host writes it; a controller updates its control to it. A worker never writes it for a value a controller's param_set gave it, and a worker that writes none changes nothing: the daemon adds no line of its own |

The relay rules:

- VERBATIM: every line a worker writes on its feedback port goes out on the daemon's feedback port as the worker wrote it: output_set, param_set, data_finish and the rest of mod-host's feedback, and a line the daemon does not know
- INSTANCE: the instance number in a relayed line is already the controller's: add hands it to the worker unchanged, so nothing in a line is rewritten
- ORDER: a worker's lines go out in the order it wrote them, and what a worker wrote before it died goes out before its worker_died event; an instance lives in one worker at a time, so its lines keep their order across a respawn; the lines of different workers interleave
- SUBSCRIPTION: monitor_output is in the ledger, one line per output, until monitor_output_off or the end of the connection that set it takes the line out, and param_monitor as it was sent; a respawn replays them after the add, so a respawned instance reports the same outputs, each once, starting again from its first value
- HANDSHAKE: output_data_ready names no instance and goes to every worker; each worker's data_finish is relayed
- WINDOW: show_external_ui and hide_external_ui go to the worker that holds the instance and its resp comes back unchanged; the window is the worker's, on the display session of the daemon's environment (WAYLAND_DISPLAY, else DISPLAY), which every worker inherits; a daemon with neither refuses both with -902 hosting.window.no-display and sends the worker nothing; the ledger keeps the latest of the two per instance, so a respawn shows again a window that was shown
- NO_CONTROLLER: with no feedback port, or no controller on it, a line is dropped, as mod-host drops it; the daemon reads every worker's feedback all the time, so no worker waits on it

### Host settings

- TEMPO: the tempo, the metre and the transport a controller sets (mod-host's set_bpm, set_bpb, transport and transport_sync) are kept, the latest line of each as it was sent, in the order they were last sent
- REPLAY: a worker is handed them before anything else: a respawned one before its first add, and a worker started later, of a new placement, as well; a worker's refusal of one is written to stderr and is no failure
- GRAMMAR: a line whose words are not that command's grammar is passed on and not kept

### Node metadata

The JACK metadata a worker sets on the uuid of each client it opens for an instance, on jackd and on PipeWire. The client's name stays `effect_<instance>`; a client shows the pretty name and matches a hosted node on the instance key, never on the name's prefix. The value is a printf format, filled by the arguments in order.

| name | key | value | arguments | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pretty_name` | `http://jackaudio.org/metadata/pretty-name` | `%s (%d)` | plugin name, instance | the name a graph client shows for the node: the plugin's name from its descriptor and the instance |
| `instance` | `http://openmixer.org/ns/plugin-hostd#instance` | `%d` | instance | the instance the node hosts, which a client matches a hosted node on |
| `labelled_name` | `http://jackaudio.org/metadata/pretty-name` | `%s: %s (%d)` | label, plugin name, instance | the pretty-name of a node a client has labelled (node_label): the label, the plugin's name and the instance, in place of pretty_name until the label is cleared |

Reply codes
-----------

mod-host's parse refusals (`protocol.h`): -1 PROTOCOL_NOT_FOUND (not found); -2 PROTOCOL_MANY_ARGUMENTS (many arguments); -3 PROTOCOL_FEW_ARGUMENTS (few arguments); -4 PROTOCOL_INVALID_ARGUMENT (invalid argument).

mod-host's reply codes (`host-errors.h`): 0 SUCCESS; -1 ERR_INSTANCE_INVALID; -2 ERR_INSTANCE_ALREADY_EXISTS; -3 ERR_INSTANCE_NON_EXISTS; -4 ERR_INSTANCE_UNLICENSED; -101 ERR_HOST_INVALID_URI; -102 ERR_HOST_INSTANTIATION; -103 ERR_HOST_INVALID_PARAM_SYMBOL; -104 ERR_HOST_INVALID_PRESET_URI; -105 ERR_HOST_CANT_LOAD_STATE; -101 ERR_LV2_INVALID_URI; -102 ERR_LV2_INSTANTIATION; -103 ERR_LV2_INVALID_PARAM_SYMBOL; -104 ERR_LV2_INVALID_PRESET_URI; -105 ERR_LV2_CANT_LOAD_STATE; -201 ERR_JACK_CLIENT_CREATION; -202 ERR_JACK_CLIENT_ACTIVATION; -203 ERR_JACK_CLIENT_DEACTIVATION; -204 ERR_JACK_PORT_REGISTER; -205 ERR_JACK_PORT_CONNECTION; -206 ERR_JACK_PORT_DISCONNECTION; -207 ERR_JACK_VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE; -301 ERR_ASSIGNMENT_ALREADY_EXISTS; -302 ERR_ASSIGNMENT_INVALID_OP; -303 ERR_ASSIGNMENT_LIST_FULL; -304 ERR_ASSIGNMENT_FAILED; -305 ERR_ASSIGNMENT_UNUSED; -401 ERR_CONTROL_CHAIN_UNAVAILABLE; -402 ERR_ABLETON_LINK_UNAVAILABLE; -403 ERR_HMI_UNAVAILABLE; -404 ERR_EXTERNAL_UI_UNAVAILABLE; -901 ERR_MEMORY_ALLOCATION; -902 ERR_INVALID_OPERATION.

The codes omx-clap-host answers too (omx-clap-core's `reply.host.*`):

| resp | code | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| -1 | `reply.host.instance-invalid` | mod-host's ERR_INSTANCE_INVALID: an instance number outside the host's table |
| -3 | `reply.host.instance-non-exists` | mod-host's ERR_INSTANCE_NON_EXISTS: an instance no add made |
| -103 | `reply.host.param-symbol-invalid` | mod-host's ERR_LV2_INVALID_PARAM_SYMBOL: a symbol that is not a parameter param_set takes, the plugin's own bypass included |
| -508 | `reply.host.pin-absent` | a layout pin in a scheme this host does not know, refused as no pin at all |
| -510 | `reply.host.pin-layout-mismatch` | the add of an instance whose layout after init is not the one pin_expect named: the plugin is not activated |
| -511 | `reply.host.no-param-contract` | the host holds no checked unit and scale for this parameter: the controller falls back to the layout the scan gives |
| -513 | `reply.host.no-note-input` | the instance's plugin takes no notes |
| -514 | `reply.host.notes-by-jack` | the instance's worker takes no notes on its socket (mod-host): the plugin is played through its jack MIDI input |
| -517 | `reply.host.note-queue-full` | the worker has no room for the line's notes before its next block: nothing of it is kept, and the line may be sent again |
| -901 | `reply.host.memory-allocation` | mod-host's ERR_MEMORY_ALLOCATION: the reply could not be built |
| -902 | `reply.host.invalid-operation` | mod-host's ERR_INVALID_OPERATION: a word outside the verb's grammar, or a verb the host refuses on purpose |

The codes the daemon adds:

| resp | name | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| -501 | `PLACEMENT_INVALID` | placement invalid: not a placement, or not valid here, as a pool:<name> for a plugin of a format whose pin holds only in a world of the plugin's own, while require_pins is on |
| -502 | `NO_BACKEND` | no worker program for the scheme |
| -503 | `WORKER_SPAWN` | the worker is not up: the spawn failed, or it is in backoff; ask again after instance_restored |
| -504 | `REPLAY` | the name of a refused replay, never a reply: a replayed add that its pin or the worker refuses is announced by the instance_replay_refused event with the refusal's own code, and written to stderr with this one and the step that refused it |
| -505 | `GAVE_UP` | the storm bound is spent for that placement |
| -506 | `NO_SUCH_WORKER` | no such worker |
| -507 | `VERB_DROPPED` | the worker died on this very command and the daemon dropped it: it is not replayed, and the instance_verb_dropped event names it; or it died on, or did not answer in rpc_timeout_ms, the pin_expect of an add, which is then never forwarded |
| -508 | `PIN_ABSENT` | pin_mode strict and the plugin has no pin, or its layout pin is in a scheme this version does not know: add is refused and no worker sees it |
| -509 | `PIN_BINARY_MISMATCH` | a pinned file is missing or its SHA-256 differs, or the plugin's manifest names a file the pin does not hold: add is refused and no worker sees it |
| -510 | `PIN_LAYOUT_MISMATCH` | the worker found the parameter layout after init differs from the layout pin: the instance is destroyed before activate |
| -511 | `NO_PARAM_CONTRACT` | the host holds no checked unit and scale for this parameter: fall back to qualification |
| -512 | `LV2_ADAPTER_REFUSED` | the lv2-clap worker's LV2 adapter cannot run this plugin (MIDI it does not feed, a required feature it lacks, a layout it does not take): the worker answered the add -102, the lv2_adapter_refused event carries the hosting.* code of that reply; the plugin is never handed to another host; a plugin no bundle of the worker's world holds is no refusal: the worker's -101 is answered |
| -513 | `NO_NOTE_INPUT` | the instance's plugin takes no notes (an effect): its worker answers note_on, note_off and all_notes_off with this code |
| -514 | `NOTES_BY_JACK` | the instance's worker takes no notes on its socket (mod-host): the daemon answers the note verbs and note_input with this code, and the plugin is played through its jack MIDI input with connect |
| -515 | `NO_PRESET_LIST` | the instance's worker cannot list the plugin's presets (mod-host): the daemon answers preset_list and preset_get with this code; preset_load still takes a preset the controller knows |
| -516 | `PIN_REFUSED` | the plugin's pin carries verdict=refused: its files are the ones that failed qualification, so add is refused and no worker sees it, and a replayed add is refused the same way; files that differ from the pin answer (-509) first. A pins_dir pin of that verdict is not overridden by the host's pins: pin_set of its plugin answers this code. Only the user's pin_accept under pin_mode first-use loads it, alone |
| -517 | `NOTE_QUEUE_FULL` | the instance's worker has no room for this note_on, note_off or all_notes_off before its next block: the line was not taken and nothing of it is kept; the controller may send it again |
| -518 | `CHAIN_UNKNOWN_INSTANCE` | a member of chain is an instance no add made: the chain is not declared |
| -519 | `CHAIN_DUPLICATE` | an instance is named twice in one chain: the chain is not declared |
| -520 | `CHAIN_INSTANCE_BUSY` | a member of chain is already in another chain: the chain is not declared; chain_clear of the other chain frees it |
| -521 | `CHAIN_MIXED_FORMAT` | the members of chain are not all run by one worker program, or are of two rows of one program and a row does not run chains in one client, so no one worker runs them: the chain is not declared |
| -522 | `NO_SUCH_CHAIN` | chain_clear or chain_get of a chain no chain declared |
| -523 | `PRESET_NOT_OFFERED` | the worker: preset_load or preset_show of a stable name the plugin does not offer, or of a plugin with no preset system and no state |
| -524 | `PRESET_INVALID` | preset_save with a file path that is not absolute or with no name, or preset_load or preset_show of a file that cannot be read, is no JSON, is of a format version other than org.openmixer.preset/1 and org.openmixer.preset/2, or breaks the format (docs/presets.md): the daemon answers it and no worker sees the file |
| -525 | `PRESET_NEEDS_STATE` | the worker: a preset file that carries state for a worker that cannot take state yet |
| -526 | `PRESET_PLUGIN_CHANGED` | the worker: the preset file's plugin id, version or fingerprint is not the instance's; nothing of it is applied |
| -527 | `LOAD_REFUSED` | the worker: the plugin refused the preset or the state its file carries |
| -544 | `PRESET_NOT_APPLIED` | the worker: the plugin took the preset and had not run once since when the host's wait for that ran out |
| -528 | `DIR_NOT_WRITABLE` | descriptor_dir or qualification_dir cannot be made or written: the daemon does not start, and says which key and which path on stderr with this code; a directory that turns read-only later makes the scan of an add write nothing, and descriptor_get and panel_get of that plugin answer this code |
| -529 | `DESCRIPTOR_ABSENT` | descriptor_get (panel_get) of a plugin that has no descriptor (panel) in descriptor_dir for its binary as it is now, and none being written: no add since it changed, or a binary that cannot be found |
| -530 | `DESCRIPTOR_PENDING` | descriptor_get (panel_get) of a plugin whose scan, started by its add, has not written its descriptor (panel) yet: ask again |
| -531 | `DESCRIPTOR_SCAN_FAILED` | descriptor_get (panel_get) of a plugin whose last scan wrote no descriptor (panel): the scanner refused the plugin, made no dump or no panel, or is not installed; the add it ran for stands, and stderr and the scan's log say why. The next add scans again |
| -532 | `NO_SUCH_PLAN` | plan_get or plan_clear of a chain no plan planned |
| -533 | `NO_RECORD` | a member of estimate that no qualification record in qualification_dir names: never a reply, the code of the member in the reply's list |
| -534 | `NO_CELL` | a member of estimate whose qualification records hold no point of the grid at that rate and quantum with a cost and a latency: never a reply, the code of the member in the reply's list |
| -535 | `UNKNOWN_PLUGIN` | a member of estimate whose uri names no plugin installed here (its format cannot tell the plugin's binary, or the binary is not there): never a reply, the code of the member in the reply's list |
| -536 | `CURVE_KIND_UNKNOWN` | curve_bind of a family with no closed form for the display's kind, or curve_points of a binding whose values pick a band shape or a head filter slope with no closed form: no curve is drawn |
| -537 | `CURVE_TERM_MISSING` | curve_points of a display with no binding, or of a binding that lacks a term the model needs (a band's frequency, shape or Q, a threshold, a ratio, a gate's range): no curve is drawn from a guess |
| -538 | `CURVE_UNIT_REFUSED` | curve_bind of a term in a unit its role does not take: nothing of the line is kept |
| -539 | `CURVE_POINTS_RANGE` | curve_points of fewer than 2 points or more than a curve carries, three anchors a drawn band counted, or of a band index past what fits |
| -540 | `DURABLE_WRITE_FAILED` | the daemon's writer thread could not write the file the verb changes (history_clear, pin_clear, pin_accept): the change is not on disk, and stderr names the path and the error |
| -541 | `WRITER_QUEUE_FULL` | the daemon's writer queue holds its most writes or bytes: the write the verb needs is refused and nothing of the verb changed; the controller may send it again |
| -542 | `CURVE_VALUE_NOT_FINITE` | curve_points of a binding whose value, as the instance holds it, is not finite, or of an instance that runs at no rate: no curve is drawn |
| -543 | `OUTPUT_NOT_MONITORED` | monitor_output_off of an output this connection did not monitor: a monitor ends with the connection that set it, and only that connection ends it earlier |
| -545 | `LABEL_INVALID` | node_label of a label longer than PHD_NODE_LABEL_MAX bytes or not UTF-8: the node keeps the label it had |

Appendix: mod-host's command reference
--------------------------------------

The "Commands (or Protocol)" section of mod-host's README (Open-Mixer/mod-host, branch freemixer, 013ac7d), kept as it
is. Copyright 2013-2026 Filipe Coelho, MOD Audio UG and the mod-host contributors, GPL-3.0-or-later.

Where it says "mod-host", read "the host": any host built on this library answers these commands. The library parses
and dispatches them; what a command does to a plugin is the host's backend (`host_backend_t`, `include/host-backend.h`).

Commands (or Protocol)
----------------------

The commands supported by mod-host are:

    add <lv2_uri> <instance_number> [client_name]
        * add an LV2 plugin encapsulated as a jack client
        e.g.: add "http://lv2plug.in/plugins/eg-amp" 0
        instance_number must be any value between 0 ~ 9990, inclusively
        client_name is optional; when omitted the jack client (and so the graph node) is
        named "effect_<instance_number>", same as always. When given, mod-host tries to
        open the jack client under that name instead -- so a host running many plugins
        shows a graph with a name per plugin instead of an undifferentiated effect_0,
        effect_1, effect_2... The name is sanitised for jack (':' is replaced with '_',
        since jack uses ':' as the client:port separator, and it is truncated to the
        running jack backend's client name limit) and, on a collision with an existing
        jack client, disambiguated by appending "_<instance_number>". If the sanitised
        name is empty, or the name still collides after the instance number is appended,
        mod-host falls back to the default "effect_<instance_number>" rather than fail
        the add.
        e.g.: add "http://lv2plug.in/plugins/eg-amp" 0 "channel1-eg-amp"

    remove <instance_number>
        * remove an LV2 plugin instance (and also the jack client)
        e.g.: remove 0
        when instance_number is -1 all plugins will be removed

    preset_load <instance_number> <preset_uri>
        * load a preset state of an effect instance
        e.g.: preset_load 0 "http://drobilla.net/plugins/mda/presets#JX10-moogcury-lite"

    preset_save <instance_number> <preset_name> <dir> <file_name>
        * save a preset state of an effect instance
        e.g.: preset_save 0 "My Preset" "/home/user/.lv2/my-presets.lv2" "mypreset.ttl"

    preset_show <preset_uri>
        * show the preset information of requested URI
        e.g.: preset_show "http://drobilla.net/plugins/mda/presets#EPiano-bright"

    connect <origin_port> <destination_port>
        * connect two jack ports
        e.g.: connect "system:capture_1" "effect_0:in"

    disconnect <origin_port> <destination_port>
        * disconnect two jack ports
        e.g.: disconnect "system:capture_1" "effect_0:in"

    bypass <instance_number> <bypass_value>
        * toggle effect processing
        e.g.: bypass 0 1
        if bypass_value = 1 bypass effect
        if bypass_value = 0 process effect

    param_set <instance_number> <param_symbol> <param_value>
        * set the value of a control port
        e.g.: param_set 0 "gain" 2.5

    param_get <instance_number> <param_symbol>
        * get the value of a control port
        e.g.: param_get 0 "gain"

    param_monitor <instance_number> <param_symbol> <cond_op> <value>
        * monitor a control port according to a condition
        e.g: param_monitor 0 "gain" ">" 2.5

    patch_set <instance_number> <property_uri> <value>
        * set the value of a control port
        e.g.: patch_set 0 "gain" 2.5

    patch_get <instance_number> <property_uri>
        * get the value of a control port
        e.g.: patch_get 0 "gain"

    licensee <instance_number>
        * get the licensee name for a commercial plugin
        e.g.: licensee 0

    monitor <addr> <port> <status>
        * open a socket port for monitoring parameter changes
        e.g: monitor localhost 12345 1
        if status = 1 start monitoring
        if status = 0 stop monitoring

    monitor_output <instance_number> <param_symbol>
        * request monitoring of an output control port (on the feedback port)
        e.g.: monitor_output 0 "meter"

    midi_learn <instance_number> <param_symbol> <minimum> <maximum>
        * start MIDI learn for a control port
        e.g.: midi_learn 0 "gain" 0.0 1.0

    midi_map <instance_number> <param_symbol> <midi_channel> <midi_cc> <minimum> <maximum>
        * map a MIDI controller to a control port
        e.g.: midi_map 0 "gain" 0 7 0.0 1.0
        a non-standard midi_cc value of 131 (0x83) is used for pitchbend

    midi_unmap <instance_number> <param_symbol>
        * unmap the MIDI controller from a control port
        e.g.: midi_unmap 0 "gain"

    monitor_midi_program <midi_channel> <enable>
        * listen to MIDI program change messages (on the feedback port)
        e.g.: monitor_midi_program 0 1

    set_midi_program_change_pedalboard_bank_channel <enable> <midi_channel>
        * set the MIDI channel which changes pedalboard banks on MIDI program change. <midi_channel> is in the range of [0,15].
        e.g.: set_midi_program_change_pedalboard_bank_channel 1 5 to enable listening for bank changes on channel 6

    set_midi_program_change_pedalboard_snapshot_channel <enable> <midi_channel>
        * set the MIDI channel which changes pedalboard snapshots on MIDI program change. <midi_channel> is in the range of [0,15].
        e.g.: set_midi_program_change_pedalboard_snapshot_channel 1 4 to enable listening for preset changes on channel 5

    cc_map <instance_number> <param_symbol> <device_id> <actuator_id> <label> <value> <minimum> <maximum> <steps> <extraflags> <unit> <scalepoints_count> <scalepoints...>
        * map a Control Chain actuator to a control port
        e.g.: cc_map 0 "gain" 0 1 "Gain" 0.0 -24.0 3.0 33 0 "dB" 0

    cc_unmap <instance_number> <param_symbol>
        * unmap the Control Chain actuator from a control port
        e.g.: cc_unmap 0 "gain"

    cc_value_set <instance_number> <param_symbol> <value>
        * set the value of a  mapped Control Chain actuator
        e.g.: cc_value_set 0 "gain" 2.5

    cv_map <instance_number> <param_symbol> <source_port_name> <minimum> <maximum> <operational-mode>
        * map a CV source port to a control port, operational-mode being one of '-', '+', 'b' or '='
        e.g.: cv_map 0 "gain" "AMS CV Source:CV Out 1" -24.0 3.0 =

    cv_unmap <instance_number> <param_symbol>
        * unmap the CV source port actuator from a control port
        e.g.: cv_unmap 0 "gain"

    cpu_load
        * return current jack cpu load

    load <file_name>
        * load a history command file
        * dummy way to save/load workspace state
        e.g.: load my_setup

    save <file_name>
        * saves the history of typed commands
        * dummy way to save/load workspace state
        e.g.: save my_setup

    bundle_add <bundle_path>
        * add a bundle to the running lv2 world
        e.g.: bundle_add "/path/to/bundle.lv2"

    bundle_remove <bundle_path> <resource>
        * remove a bundle from the running lv2 world
        e.g.: bundle_remove "/path/to/bundle.lv2" ""

    feature_enable <feature> <enable>
        * enable or disable a feature
        * feature can be one of "aggregated-midi", "freewheeling" or "processing"
        * the "aggregated-midi" feature requires the use of jack2 and mod-midi-merger to be installed system-wide
        e.g.: feature_enable link 1

    set_bpm <beats_per_minute>
        * set the global beats per minute transport value
        e.g.: set_bpm 120

    set_bpb <beats_per_bar>
        * set the global beats per bar transport value
        e.g.: set_bpb 4

    transport <rolling> <beats_per_bar> <beats_per_minute>
        * change the global transport state
        e.g.: transport 1 4 120

    transport_sync <mode>
        * change the transport sync mode
        * mode can be one of "none", "link" or "midi"
        e.g.: transport_sync "midi"

    output_data_ready
        * report feedback port ready for more messages

    track_info <instance_number> <name> <color> [bus|return|master]
        * pass the name and color of the mixer track the instance sits on, color as #RRGGBB or - for none
        * an LV2 plugin has no way to receive them, so mod-host answers -902
        e.g.: track_info 0 "Kick In" #FF8000

    remote_pages <instance_number>
        * get the number of remote-control pages of the plugin (8 parameters per page); 0 for an LV2 plugin
        e.g.: remote_pages 0

    remote_page_get <instance_number> <page_index>
        * get one remote-control page: resp 0 <page_id> <section_name> <page_name> <symbol> x8, - for an empty slot
        e.g.: remote_page_get 0 0

    param_info <instance_number> <param_symbol>
        * get what a control means: resp 0 <unit> <scale> <minimum> <maximum> <default> <step> <stable_symbol>
        * unit is an LV2 unit name (db, hz, ms, ...) or none, scale is linear, log or stepped, step 0 is continuous
        e.g.: param_info 0 "gain"

    help
        * show a help message

    quit
        bye!

For each effect added one client on JACK will be created. The names of clients
follow the standard: effect_\<instance_number\>

If a valid command is executed a response is given as following:

    resp <status> [value]

If status is a negative number an error has occurred. The table below shows the number of each error.

| status  | error                            |
| --------|----------------------------------|
| -1      | ERR\_INSTANCE\_INVALID           |
| -2      | ERR\_INSTANCE\_ALREADY\_EXISTS   |
| -3      | ERR\_INSTANCE\_NON\_EXISTS       |
| -4      | ERR\_INSTANCE\_UNLICENSED        |
| -101    | ERR\_LV2\_INVALID\_URI           |
| -102    | ERR\_LV2\_INSTANTIATION          |
| -103    | ERR\_LV2\_INVALID\_PARAM\_SYMBOL |
| -104    | ERR\_LV2\_INVALID\_PRESET\_URI   |
| -105    | ERR\_LV2\_CANT\_LOAD\_STATE      |
| -201    | ERR\_JACK\_CLIENT\_CREATION      |
| -202    | ERR\_JACK\_CLIENT\_ACTIVATION    |
| -203    | ERR\_JACK\_CLIENT\_DEACTIVATION  |
| -204    | ERR\_JACK\_PORT\_REGISTER        |
| -205    | ERR\_JACK\_PORT\_CONNECTION      |
| -206    | ERR\_JACK\_PORT\_DISCONNECTION   |
| -207    | ERR\_JACK\_VALUE\_OUT\_OF\_RANGE |
| -301    | ERR\_ASSIGNMENT\_ALREADY\_EXISTS |
| -302    | ERR\_ASSIGNMENT\_INVALID\_OP     |
| -303    | ERR\_ASSIGNMENT\_LIST\_FULL      |
| -304    | ERR\_ASSIGNMENT\_FAILED          |
| -304    | ERR\_ASSIGNMENT\_UNUSED          |
| -401    | ERR\_CONTROL\_CHAIN\_UNAVAILABLE |
| -402    | ERR\_LINK\_UNAVAILABLE           |
| -403    | ERR\_HMI\_UNAVAILABLE            |
| -404    | ERR\_EXTERNAL\_UI\_UNAVAILABLE   |
| -901    | ERR\_MEMORY\_ALLOCATION          |
| -902    | ERR\_INVALID\_OPERATION          |

A status zero or positive means that the command was executed successfully.
In case of the add command, the status returned is the instance number.
The value field exists for the param_get, remote_page_get and param_info commands.

When the plugin changes its remote-control pages, the feedback port gets:

    remote_pages_changed <instance_number>
